[Sassolite](/wiki/Sassolite "Sassolite")

Borax in its mineral form (then known as tincal) first saw use as a glaze, beginning in [China](/wiki/China "China") circa 300 AD. Some crude borax traveled westward, and was apparently mentioned by the alchemist [Jabir ibn Hayyan](/wiki/Jabir_ibn_Hayyan "Jabir ibn Hayyan") around 700 AD. [Marco Polo](/wiki/Marco_Polo "Marco Polo") brought some glazes back to Italy in the 13th century. [Georgius Agricola](/wiki/Georgius_Agricola "Georgius Agricola"), in around 1600, reported the use of borax as a flux in [metallurgy](/wiki/Metallurgy "Metallurgy"). In 1777, [boric acid](/wiki/Boric_acid "Boric acid") was recognized in the hot springs ([soffioni](/wiki/Soffioni "Soffioni")) near [Florence](/wiki/Florence "Florence"), Italy, at which point it became known as *sal sedativum*, with ostensible medical benefits. The mineral was named [sassolite](/wiki/Sassolite "Sassolite") after [Sasso Pisano](/wiki/Sasso_Pisano "Sasso Pisano") in Italy. Sasso was the main source of [European](/wiki/Europe "Europe") borax from 1827 to 1872, when [American](/wiki/United_States "United States") sources replaced it.[[18]](#cite_note-borates-18)[[19]](#cite_note-boron-19) Boron compounds were rarely used until the late 1800s when [Francis Marion Smith](/wiki/Francis_Marion_Smith "Francis Marion Smith")'s [Pacific Coast Borax Company](/wiki/Pacific_Coast_Borax_Company "Pacific Coast Borax Company") first popularized and produced them in volume at low cost.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

From 1997 to 2004, Dell steadily grew and it gained market share from competitors even during industry slumps, with its fastest growth occurring in the early 2000s. During the same period, rival PC vendors such as [Compaq](/wiki/Compaq "Compaq"), [Gateway](/wiki/Gateway,_Inc. "Gateway, Inc."), [IBM](/wiki/IBM_Aptiva "IBM Aptiva"), [Packard Bell](/wiki/Packard_Bell "Packard Bell"), and [AST Research](/wiki/AST_Research "AST Research") struggled and eventually left the market or were bought out.[[31]](#cite_note-ZDA-31) Dell surpassed Compaq to become the largest PC manufacturer in 1999.[[32]](#cite_note-32) Operating costs made up only 10 percent of Dell's $35 billion in revenue in 2002 (equivalent to $58,170,000,000 in 2024), compared with 21 percent of revenue at Hewlett-Packard, 25 percent at Gateway, and 46 percent at Cisco.[[33]](#cite_note-33) In 2002, when Compaq merged with Hewlett-Packard (the fourth-place PC maker), the newly combined Hewlett-Packard took the top spot for a time but struggled and Dell soon regained its lead.[[4]](#cite_note-bw1103-4)

In 2002, Dell expanded its product line to include televisions, [handhelds](/wiki/Handhelds "Handhelds"), digital audio players, and [printers](/wiki/Printer_(computing) "Printer (computing)"). Chairman and CEO Michael Dell had repeatedly blocked President and COO Kevin Rollins's attempt to lessen the company's heavy dependency on PCs, which Rollins wanted to fix by acquiring EMC Corporation; a move that would eventually occur over 12 years later.[[34]](#cite_note-CNNMoney-dilemma-34)

In 2003, at the annual company meeting, the stockholders approved changing the company name to "Dell Inc." to recognize the company's expansion beyond computers.[[35]](#cite_note-Dell-Inc-May-2003-PRE-14A-35)

In 2004, the company announced that it would build a new assembly-plant near [Winston-Salem](/wiki/Winston-Salem,_North_Carolina "Winston-Salem, North Carolina"), [North Carolina](/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina"); the city and county provided Dell with $37.2 million in incentive packages; the state provided approximately $250 million

Also during that off-season, the Heat would select [Bam Adebayo](/wiki/Bam_Adebayo "Bam Adebayo") during the [2017 NBA draft](/wiki/2017_NBA_draft "2017 NBA draft") and on February 8, 2018, the Miami Heat would acquire Dwyane Wade back from the Cleveland Cavaliers.[[37]](#cite_note-37) Wade willed the Heat to a game two win against the Philadelphia 76ers in the first round of the [2018 playoffs](/wiki/2018_NBA_playoffs "2018 NBA playoffs"), but the team would lose the series in five games. After the [AFL–NFL merger](/wiki/AFL%E2%80%93NFL_merger "AFL–NFL merger") was completed in 1970, three franchises—the Cowboys, [Miami Dolphins](/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"), and Steelers—would go on to dominate the 1970s, winning a combined eight Super Bowls between them in the decade, with the Steelers winning four of the eight.

The Baltimore Colts, now a member of the AFC, would start the decade by defeating the Cowboys in Super Bowl V, a game which is the only Super Bowl to date in which a player from the losing team won the Super Bowl MVP (Cowboys' linebacker [Chuck Howley](/wiki/Chuck_Howley "Chuck Howley")).[[25]](#cite_note-27)[[26]](#cite_note-28) Beginning with this Super Bowl, all Super Bowls have served as the NFL's championship game.
